chains.earliest_control: phishing-resistant MFA required for all users
chains.name: Credential phishing to payment diversion

steps.text: An adversary-in-the-middle phishing page relays the password and SMS code of one of the two staff who use SMS: 2-Step Verification is not enforced and phishing-resistant MFA is not required (GWS.COMMONCONTROLS.1.1v1, GWS.COMMONCONTROLS.1.3v1; A2).
The stolen session lasts 14 days (GWS.COMMONCONTROLS.4.1v1; B2). Automatic forwarding is off, so the attacker reads in place and adds a filter that archives the client's replies, hiding the thread.
The attacker alters a payment instruction in a live client thread, and the client pays the attacker's account (F1).

chains.earliest_control: a DMARC enforcement policy in force for the domain
chains.name: Self-spoof business email compromise

steps.text: An attacker sends mail to the bookkeeper from an outside server using the founder's own address. DMARC is at p=none (GWS.GMAIL.4.2v1; C2), so receivers apply no enforcement.
Gmail's protection against inbound mail spoofing the firm's own domain is off (GWS.GMAIL.7.3v1; C1), so the message arrives as ordinary internal mail.
The bookkeeper changes a supplier's payment details on the instruction, with no call-back step (F1).

chains.earliest_control: "anyone with the link" disabled where external sharing is allowed
chains.name: Link sharing exposure

steps.text: Six client folders are shared "anyone with the link" (GWS.DRIVEDOCS.1.5v1; D2), and sharing outside the organization has no allowlist (GWS.DRIVEDOCS.1.1v1; D1).
A client forwards a folder link beyond the client's own staff; whoever holds the link opens the folder without signing in.
The folder's contents surface months later outside both firms, with no record of who opened them.
